Operating Systems
CS 301 · IIT Gandhinagar · Semester I, 2019–20
CS 301 covers the three pieces of a modern operating system: virtualisation of the CPU and of memory, concurrency, and persistence. Lectures follow Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces, weekly labs put the ideas into practice, and students wrote an OS zine and carried out a group project.

  InstructorProf. Nipun Batra
  Emailnipun.batra@iitgn.ac.in
  LecturesTuesday, Thursday and Friday, 11:00 am–12:00 noon, AB7/102
  LabsMonday, 10:00 am–12:00 noon, AB7/109
  Teaching assistants3 TAs
  TextbookOperating Systems: Three Easy Pieces



Course record
This offering ran from August to November 2019. Its slides, lab material and class code remain available.

  Classes37
  LabsWeekly labs, a lab quiz and a lab exam
  QuizzesPapers for quizzes 1 and 2
  CodeCode used in classes
  Virtual machineUbuntu VirtualBox image

All dates


Lectures

  1–8Processes and CPU scheduling8 lectures
  9–20Memory virtualisation12 lectures
  21–32Concurrency12 lectures
  33–37Persistence5 lectures


  All 37 classes




Questions
Is there a mid-semester exam?No. The end-semester exam carries 10%; most of the grade comes from four quizzes, two lab exams, the project and the homework. See Grading.
Is there a project?Yes: a project in groups of four, worth 20%. Teams submit a timeline, give phase I updates and present a final demo. See the project ideas.
What is the OS zine?A zine on an operating-systems topic, in the style of Julia Evans's zines. It is worth 2% and was due on 20 November.
Can I ask for my score to be revised?Only if a question was left unchecked or the marks were totalled incorrectly.
What do I need for the labs and homework?A Linux environment. An Ubuntu VirtualBox image is provided, and the code used in classes is on GitHub.

References
Main textbook:

  Remzi H. Arpaci-Dusseau and Andrea C. Arpaci-Dusseau, Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces (free online)
